safety/readonly.py:576 raises UnsafeSqlError(f"could not parse SQL: {e}") on parse failure. ReadOnlyGuardRunner.run_sql (safety/__init__.py:96-100) re-raises it as "refusing to execute non-SELECT SQL: could not parse SQL: ...", keeping the substring. RunSqlTool (agent/tools/run_sql.py:190-191) catches Exception and sets result_for_llm to "Error executing query: {e}", so the model sees the exact phrase 'could not parse SQL'. The RLS variant (rls.py:226) reads "could not parse SQL for row-level security", wrapped at safety/__init__.py:176 as "...could not be applied: could not parse SQL for row-level security: ...", which also contains the phrase. The prompt text at default.py:112 matches.

The two-attempt limit appears only as prompt text (src/sqllens/agent/core/system_prompt/default.py:112, 'Make at most two corrected attempts for one failing query'). A search of src for attempt/retry/retries/max_retr/consecutive/failure_count found no run_sql or SQL-failure counter. The only counter in agent.py is consecutive_argument_failures (agent.py:664, 1050-1054, MAX_CONSECUTIVE_ARGUMENT_FAILURES=3). It counts rounds in which every tool call failed on invalid or truncated arguments, so it is not a count of corrected SQL attempts. It resets on any round that is not all argument failures, and it does not track SQL text rejections. The recovery/base.py 'attempt' parameter is only a docstring example and a hook signature, and nothing in the agent loop passes a SQL-correction count to it. Hostile input traced: a run_sql that fails 3+ times for SQL text. Nothing in agent.py stops it, because those failures are not argument failures. That matches the doc claim. The docs (tool-scratch-storage.md:112) correctly say the limit is prompt-only.

docs/external/getting-started.md:62 says that when the first attempt fails (including the database rejecting unsupported syntax), the agent corrects the query and retries, up to two corrected attempts. src/sqllens/agent/core/system_prompt/default.py:112 (Tool Errors) tells the model: if run_sql fails because the database rejected the query text (syntax error, unknown table/column/function) or 'could not parse SQL', correct and rerun, 'at most two corrected attempts for one failing query'. This is a prompt string only; a grep of that file for corrected/attempt/retry shows no code-level counter, so the limit is a prompt instruction and not enforced there.

readonly.py:215-216 is_introspection_query returns True whenever first_sql_keyword(sql, dialect)=="SHOW" (before any parse), so a MySQL structural SHOW is classified as introspection. Catalog tables for each engine are also covered (readonly.py:121-125: information_schema shared, mysql/sys/performance_schema for MySQL, sqlite_/pragma_ for SQLite, pg_catalog/pg_ for Postgres). The docstring (192-194) states the formatter uses it to keep a catalog lookup's success from clearing an earlier failure, matching tools.md:148. Structural SHOW subkinds are allowed by the read-only guard (readonly.py:273-280, 625-631), so the prompt allowing it is consistent.
